transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-15
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez, Samir Patel, Lydia Chen (Redwood) — Dr. Megan Ortiz, James Holloway, Priya Nair, Carlos Ruiz (NewLeaf)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect):
Ava: quick runthrough of onboarding plan; ask about infra and compliance; set pilot scope.

[00:00] Ava Martinez: okay, hey everyone thanks for jumping on, really excited to kick this off with NewLeaf, I'm Ava from Redwood Account team, with Samir and Lydia from CS and SE, can you quickly intro?
[00:18] Dr. Megan Ortiz: hi all, Megan here, CTO at NewLeaf, we've got James on data and Priya on compliance. Carlos is here for infra.
[00:27] James Holloway: hey, quick note — we've been evaluating a couple of vendors, so looking to get a pilot up in the next 3 weeks if possible.
[00:34] Ava Martinez: great, that's the goal. High level we want a 4-6 week onboarding with a 2-week pilot phase, depends on infra but that's our standard.
[00:45] Samir Patel: hi, glad to be here, I'll own the cadence and onboarding plan, make sure we have milestones and success metrics.
[00:51] Lydia Chen: and I'll run the connectivity tests and help with model mapping, infra requirements — especially if you're looking at private or VPC deployment.
[01:02] Priya Nair: quick question — our compliance team will need SOC2 and KMS details, and audit logs, is that something Redwood provides for private deployments?
[01:12] Lydia Chen: yes, we provide SOC2 documentation, KMS/HSM integration notes, and audit logs — there's a private deployment package that includes guidance. I'll share the checklist.
[01:22] Carlos Ruiz: do you support direct VPC peering or do we need a NAT and tunnel? We prefer not to expose anything public.
[01:30] Lydia Chen: we support both VPC peering and private connectivity via VPN; peering is preferred for lower latency. We'll send an infra checklist.
[01:39] Dr. Megan Ortiz: great — latency is key for our use, we have 99th p95 around 350 ms tolerable for inter-service calls. Need to understand per-call cost and options for caching.
[01:51] Ava Martinez: got it, we'll surface recommendations: hosted vs dedicated vs private — for NewLeaf it sounds like private with dedicated pools may make sense for predictable latency and data isolation.
[02:05] James Holloway: can you explain the quantization and cost tradeoffs? We're running embeddings and chat assistants, so token volume could get high.
[02:15] Lydia Chen: sure — we do model quantization recommendations per workload; embeddings are cheaper typically, chat with longer contexts cost more. There's an Optimize tool that suggests batching and KV cache options to reduce per-token costs.
[02:31] James Holloway: the Optimize tool — is that part of the console or separate?
[02:35] Ava Martinez: it's part of Redwood Console, shows token-level costs and suggestions — we'll include screenshots.
[02:42] [crosstalk] Priya Nair: and for retention policies — can we set customer data to never be stored in hosted mode?
[02:49] Samir Patel: yes, with private deployments you control retention and data stays in your VPC, hosted has redact/retention controls but you prefer private for strict requirements.
[02:59] Carlos Ruiz: one practical thing: we run on AWS us-west-2, want to keep everything in that region; do you have pre-baked AMIs / helm charts?
[03:08] Lydia Chen: we provide helm charts and a private control plane package; our ops docs include region tips. We'll share the repo access for the on-prem pacakage.
[03:18] Dr. Megan Ortiz: what's the typical time to first token for private deploy? i.e. how long until we can run the pilot?
[03:27] Samir Patel: from kick-off to pilot often 2-4 weeks — depends on infra readiness and compliance review, so 3 weeks is a reasonable target.
[03:35] Ava Martinez: let's line up dates: action item for Samir to send a milestone plan after this call.
[03:42] [00:04] James Holloway: ok, sounds good.
[03:46] Ava Martinez: Lydia — can you talk through the initial connectivity test?
[03:50] Lydia Chen: yep, test steps: 1) open outbound to Redwood control plane endpoints — we supply FQDNs, 2) set up peering or VPN, 3) run a small inference job to validate model selection and kv/prefix caching, 4) verify KMS integration. I'll share a checklist.
[04:14] Carlos Ruiz: for KMS, we need an architecture note — does Redwood support customer-managed keys in KMS?
[04:21] Lydia Chen: yes, we support AWS KMS customer-managed keys for encryption at rest, we'll link the integration guide.
[04:28] Priya Nair: also need data access controls and RBAC — can Redwood integrate with our SSO via SAML?
[04:35] Samir Patel: absolutely — SSO via SAML/Okta is supported, RBAC roles can map to your groups. We'll share sample config.
[04:44] Dr. Megan Ortiz: any gotchas on the audit logs retention? We need 1 year of logs for compliance.
[04:50] Lydia Chen: audit logs can be exported to your storage, retention is configurable — we'll include that in the SOC2 notes.
[04:57] [05:10] Ava Martinez: switching to pilot scope — what does success look like for NewLeaf?
[05:16] Dr. Megan Ortiz: for pilot we need 1) integration with our internal triage assistant, 2) latency under 400ms p95 for 80% of traffic, 3) cost estimate for steady-state. Also an initial data security signoff.
[05:29] James Holloway: plus we want to validate embedding accuracy on our dataset and measure recall for top-3 retrieval.
[05:36] Lydia Chen: ok so pilot tasks: connector to triage assistant, run embedding evaluation on sample dataset, measure latencies and tail. We'll set benchmarks.
[05:46] Ava Martinez: timeline proposal — week 1: infra and security docs exchanged + connectivity test; week 2: deploy model and run smoke tests; week 3-4: pilot evaluation and metrics, then review and rollout planning.
[06:01] Priya Nair: can we add gating for compliance before pilot starts? We'd like security signoff after docs are reviewed, otherwise won't run sample data.
[06:09] Samir Patel: yes, we'll make compliance signoff a milestone before any prod-like data is used.
[06:15] Carlos Ruiz: what about backups and DR? Do you have recommended strategies?
[06:21] Lydia Chen: yes — we recommend snapshotting model artifacts and KV caches to your S3, and we can configure multi-AZ redundancy for Dedicated pools. We'll send DR docs.
[06:32] [07:00] James Holloway: pricing question — do you charge per-token only or is there an infra reservation for private/dedicated?
[07:08] Ava Martinez: hosted is usage-based, dedicated/reserved capacity has a monthly commitment plus lower per-token. Private deployments usually have a platform fee and then compute costs. We'll send a tailored pricing sheet.
[07:19] Dr. Megan Ortiz: okay also want to know if you support model rollbacks and version pinning — we need to pin to a specific model version during pilot.
[07:26] Lydia Chen: absolutely — model versioning and rollout controls (canary, A/B, automatic fallback to smaller models) are built into the deployment layer.
[07:35] Priya Nair: auditability — can we get token-level logs for a given session for debugging (PII redaction required)?
[07:44] Samir Patel: yes, logs can be retention-configured and redaction filters applied. We'll document the filters.
[07:53] Ava Martinez: quick note — we'll avoid sending PII during initial tests until compliance signs off.
[07:58] [08:30] Carlos Ruiz: network ip ranges for whitelisting?
[08:33] Lydia Chen: we'll provide list of control plane endpoints and egress ranges; for peering, you won't need egress rules.
[08:41] James Holloway: is there any pre-built connector to our triage tool? We're on a custom stack built on Node + Python.
[08:49] Lydia Chen: we have SDKs and REST endpoints, plus sample Node and Python connectors — we can share a starter repo.
[08:57] Dr. Megan Ortiz: who will be our main support contact during pilot?
[09:02] Samir Patel: Samir will be primary CSM, Lydia for technical issues, Ava for commercial/questions. There's also a support ticketing channel.
[09:11] Ava Martinez: great — let's confirm milestones now and owners.
[09:15] [09:30] — brief pause while people check calendar —
[09:36] Ava Martinez: milestone 1: exchange SOC2/KMS docs and provide infra checklist (owner: Lydia + Priya), due 2027-01-22. Milestone 2: connectivity test and small smoke deployment (owner: Carlos + Lydia), target 2027-01-20. Milestone 3: pilot run and metrics (owner: James + Samir), target end of January.
[09:58] James Holloway: sounds good.
[10:02] Priya Nair: for the SOC2 doc — can you deliver a redacted copy first? We can start review.
[10:07] Lydia Chen: yes, we'll send redacted SOC2 report and the KMS integration guide.
[10:12] [11:00] Dr. Megan Ortiz: any blockers you foresee?
[11:05] Lydia Chen: the main blocker would be network setup or strict firewall rules that prevent control plane connectivity; also delays in KMS key provisioning.
[11:13] Carlos Ruiz: we can provision KMS quickly but need the exact ARN patterns.
[11:17] Lydia Chen: we'll provide example ARNs and steps.
[11:21] Ava Martinez: anything else on governance — Priya?
[11:25] Priya Nair: just one more — need evidence of pen test results or a summary. If you have a security whitepaper, that helps.
[11:31] Samir Patel: we have a security whitepaper and pen test summary we'll share — will also provide contact for security team if you want to do a joint review.
[11:40] [12:20] James Holloway: on metrics — what instrumentation do you have to surface per-route latency and token costs?
[12:27] Lydia Chen: our Console surfaces per-route dashboards, token-level cost, traces, and you can ingest logs into your existing observability pipeline; we'll give read-only access for the pilot.
[12:36] Ava Martinez: we'll include screenshots and a short demo during the next sync.
[12:42] Dr. Megan Ortiz: are there any rate limits we should be aware of for the pilot?
[12:47] Samir Patel: default rate limits are applied, but for pilot we can provision higher quotas on dedicated/private. We'll provide guidance on throttling and autoscale.
[12:57] [14:00] Carlos Ruiz: can we test a small 256-token chat and a 2k-context embedding job?
[14:06] Lydia Chen: yes, we'll simulate both during connectivity smoke tests.
[14:12] James Holloway: do you support streaming token outputs?
[14:15] Lydia Chen: yes, streaming and function/tool calling supported; we'll note it in the integration notes.
[14:20] Ava Martinez: ok we're approaching the last 10 minutes — any final questions?
[14:27] Dr. Megan Ortiz: just to confirm — pricing and milestone plan after call?
[14:32] Ava Martinez: yes — I'll send pricing and the onboarding plan doc by Tuesday (2027-01-18).
[14:38] Priya Nair: and the redacted SOC2 and pen test summary?
[14:41] Samir Patel: Lydia will share those by Friday (2027-01-22).
[14:48] Carlos Ruiz: I'll coordinate with Lydia for the connectivity test time window next week.
[14:52] Lydia Chen: great — I'll propose time slots in the invite.
[14:55] James Holloway: sounds good.
[15:00] Ava Martinez: recap of next steps: pricing + plan from me, infra checklist + SOC2 from Lydia, Samir schedules recurring check-ins, NewLeaf to provision KMS and confirm region details.
[15:15] Dr. Megan Ortiz: thanks all, looking forward.
[15:18] Ava Martinez: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and invites.
[15:22] [End of meeting]

Notes on transcript quality: auto transcription had occasional name mismatches and punctuation issues; reviewers should treat transcript as a conversational artifact.

References shared on call: onboarding_plan_deck.pdf (link to be sent), redacted_SOC2.pdf (to be shared via secure link), infra_checklist.md (repo link), starter_code_repo (Node/Python connectors).
